_meta.indication: AKYNZEO for injection is indicated in combination with dexamethasone in adults for the prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with initial and repeat courses of highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy. It has not been studied for prevention of nausea/vomiting associated with anthracycline plus cyclophosphamide chemotherapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, stratified non-inferiority trial of a single dose of palonosetron 0.25 mg as a 30-minute IV infusion vs. a 30-second IV bolus, each with oral dexamethasone prior to HEC; noninferiority margin -15% with two-sided 99% CI.
pivotal_trials.population: Cancer patients receiving highly emetogenic chemotherapy (HEC) not including anthracycline/cyclophosphamide (AC).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of patients with complete response (CR = no emetic episode and no rescue medication) in the acute phase (0-24 hours after start of HEC).
pivotal_trials.result: CR in acute phase: 186 (82.7%) with 30-minute infusion vs. 186 (86.5%) with 30-second bolus; CMH risk difference -3.8% (99% CI -12.2, 4.7), p<0.001; lower bound above the -15% margin, so noninferiority was demonstrated.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, active-control trial comparing IV NEPA FDC (IV Akynzeo) vs. oral NEPA FDC (Akynzeo capsules) with repeat dosing over 4 chemotherapy cycles; primary objective safety, with descriptive efficacy.
pivotal_trials.population: Cancer patients receiving HEC not including AC.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Safety (primary); descriptive efficacy (complete response in acute, delayed, and overall phases).
pivotal_trials.n: 405 patients randomized (203 IV NEPA FDC, 202 oral NEPA FDC); 404 treated.
pivotal_trials.result: Similar safety between IV and oral Akynzeo arms; most frequent TEAE was neutropenia in 119 (29.5%) patients (61 [30.0%] IV vs. 58 [28.9%] oral). Not powered for efficacy.

key_safety: No new safety signals compared to approved Akynzeo capsules. Most frequent TEAE in the IV safety trial (NEPA 15-18) was neutropenia in 119 (29.5%) patients and anemia in 71 (17.6%); most frequent drug-related TEAEs in the PK dose-escalation study were headache, constipation, infusion site thrombosis, abdominal pain upper, fatigue, dizziness, and nausea. Hypersensitivity reactions (including anaphylaxis) and serotonin syndrome are labeled warnings.
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of palonosetron, a serotonin-3 (5-HT3) receptor antagonist, and fosnetupitant, a prodrug of netupitant, which is a substance P/neurokinin-1 (NK-1) receptor antagonist. Palonosetron prevents nausea/vomiting in the acute phase and NK-1 antagonism addresses delayed emesis mediated by substance P.
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of two small molecules: fosnetupitant, a prodrug of netupitant, and palonosetron).

rems.type: No risk management strategies beyond product labeling are recommended.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected for a drug of this class.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under a Standard (not Priority) review classification.

summary.text: Standard NDA 210493 for Akynzeo (fosnetupitant/palonosetron) for injection, submitted and received 04/20/2017 under section 505(b) of the FDCA, approved on first cycle. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority review designations were noted; the application was not referred to an advisory committee. Efficacy was supported by bridging to the approved oral Akynzeo (bioequivalence of the netupitant component via PNET-12-23) plus the noninferiority trial PALO 15-17 establishing that the 30-minute palonosetron infusion retains efficacy, with safety supported by NEPA 15-18.
